title: Discreet Branches
description: A datapack that affects the generation of the world, entities, recipes, items and dangers in a very different way from the Vanilla game.
body:
## Discreet Branches

There's something... wrong in this world.  
It seems almost empty.  
What happened to its wildlife?

## Some Changes

- Neither animals nor structures spawn here, so killing and pillaging are not viable methods of getting food.
- Sleeping doesn't skip the night, it just makes it 8x shorter with the cost of unforseable consequences.
- There are new tools, armor and tiers: wooden (only tools), stone (only tools), copper (+ lapis-lazuli), iron (+ emerald), gold (+ redstone), diamond (+ quartz and netherite).
- Added 10 new foods.
- Changed the recipe of some items such as anvils and rails (both now use copper).
- Simpler enchanting sistem.
- The amount of ores increases the further down you go.
- In the Overworld, some biomes were modified (e.g. Windswept and Old Growth biomes, Desert, Savanna Plateau etc.), and some were included (Nest biomes and Frozen Sky).
- The Nether received a generation overhaul, including:
  - a new biome,
  - increased world height to 192 blocks,
  - 1 new ore
  - and water: yes, you can now place water in the Nether! But it can be poisonous, so be careful.

## Creatures

- Your new enemies are only visible through particles, so be aware of your surroundings and any noises you hear.
- Tall flowers, crops and amulets can be used to "reveal" enemies (make them slightly more visible and less resistant).
- They can break blocks you placed when unrevealed (such as stairs, slabs, redstone related blocks, doors, trapdoors etc.).
- Some enemies may drop totems, serving as bonus attributes.

## A Change of Pace

The two things this datapack offers the most is a greater focus on farming (for food and safety) and a new ambience of the unknown, with 30 new and uncanny remixes, invisible monsters that will hunt you down and much more to come.

## Recommendations

Do not use this datapack in a previously generated world, as it changes a lot of the world generation.
> Planting crops in alternating rows can boost their growth speed. (Minecraft Wiki trivia)
